text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Finance Minister Theo Waigel, citing the need to continue discussions about his 1997 and 1998 budgets, will skip this week's Group of Seven (G7) economic summit.
- Opposition Social Democrat (SPD) leader Oskar Lafontaine says his party will not agree to the tax reform plans of the ruling coalition.
- Michael Steiner, the international community's deputy High Representative in Bosnia, calls for international troops to extend their stay in the country beyond June 1998.
- Chancellor Helmut Kohl calls for the protection of freedom and unity in remembrance of the popular uprising in the former communist East Germany on June 17, 1953.
- The SPD calls for the European Investment Bank (EIB) to finance a 20-billion-mark jobs programme.
HANDELSBLATT
- German television channel RTL must pay a 20.1 million mark fine for a violation of advertising rules.
- Crude oil prices under pressure again after sharp climb in first third of the year.
- Bundesbank says dispute with Bonn over revaluation of gold reserves is over.
- Waigel says will not be going to G7 in Denver and will stay at home and tackle budget problems instead.
- Commerzbank settles its feud with German tax officials and agrees to pay back-tax of around 450 million marks.
- Junior coalition partners the liberal Free Democrats say Germany does not have to precisely fulfill three percent budget deficit to GDP Maastricht criterion.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- FDP leader Wolfgang Gerhardt says Germany could make first round of EMU members even with a budget deficit at 3.1 percent of GDP.
- Waigel says he won't be going to Denver for G7.
- Association of state employees criticises plans by Interior Minister Manfred Kanther for them to contribute to pensions, whereas SDP in broad agreement with plan.
- Federal Labour Office says wages in Germany have definitely not risen too sharply in the last few years.
DIE WELT
- Waigel calls off trip to Denver for G7.
- FDP warns against a delay to EMU.
- North Rhine-Westphalia economics minister Wolfgang Clement due to win a place in SPD shadow cabinet.
